privacy_intro: *** LingoLinq LLC ("LingoLinq," "we," "us," or "our") is deeply committed to your privacy. This Privacy Policy applies to our website (www.lingolinq.com) and LingoLinq's products, software, and applications (collectively, the "Product").
privacy_compliance: *** Because LingoLinq is utilized globally in educational and medical settings, we employ stringent data protection practices designed to comply with local, federal, and international regulations, including COPPA, FERPA, HIPAA, GDPR (Europe), and CCPA (California).
privacy_philosophy: *** Our core privacy philosophy is simple: we never log your private conversations, and any usage data we collect to improve our Product is strictly anonymized and requires your explicit opt-in.
privacy_agreement: *** By using the Product, you agree to the collection and use of your information as described in this policy.
privacy_guarantee_thoughts: *** LingoLinq never logs, collects, or analyzes verbatim transcripts of a communicator's conversations or specific sentences generated. Your thoughts and words are yours alone.
privacy_guarantee_separation: *** We legally and technically separate the data of the "Account Administrator" (e.g., the parent, therapist, or school district) from the "Communicator" (the AAC user). Marketing, billing data, and website cookies apply only to the Account Administrator. The Communicator's interface is free of tracking pixels, advertising, and marketing.
privacy_collect_intro: *** We collect the minimum personal information needed to operate LingoLinq securely:
privacy_collect_account: *** To establish a secure login, we collect the username, email address, and password from the Account Administrator. (We encourage organizations to use anonymized usernames for Communicators).
privacy_collect_ugc: *** Vocabulary boards, custom buttons, profile summaries, and uploaded media are stored securely for access across various devices.
privacy_collect_biometric: *** If enabled for accessibility, LingoLinq uses device sensors for head position, eye gaze, and facial expression tracking. We do not collect, store, or share Biometric Identifiers or Biometric Information. This data is processed dynamically on your local device to facilitate screen selection and is immediately discarded.
privacy_collect_analytics: *** If you explicitly opt-in, we collect automated, generalized telemetry data (e.g., how often certain app features are used). This data is stripped of personal identifiers and pooled into an aggregate format to help us improve the Product.
privacy_use_intro: *** We use the information we collect to:
privacy_use_provide: *** Provide, troubleshoot, and support your specific LingoLinq account;
privacy_use_sync: *** Sync and back up your User-Generated Content securely across your devices;
privacy_use_share: *** Facilitate secure sharing only between a communicator and their authorized support team (e.g., designated therapists or parents);
privacy_use_legal: *** Comply with legal obligations and enforce our Terms of Use.
privacy_sharing_intro: *** We only share information with authorized users (like assigned supervisors) and vetted third-party service providers who help us operate LingoLinq. These providers are bound by strict Data Processing Agreements (DPAs). No Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or Protected Health Information (PHI) is ever sent to our analytics providers.
privacy_sharing_cloud: *** for core app hosting, secure database management, and encrypted file storage;
privacy_sharing_data: *** for translating boards, and transcoding media;
privacy_sharing_analytics: *** for tracking app errors and system health (strictly anonymized data only);
privacy_sharing_support: *** for customer service and account-related email/SMS notifications (Admin only).
privacy_sharing_transfers: *** In the event that LingoLinq is involved in a merger, acquisition, sale of assets, or bankruptcy, your information may be transferred to the acquiring entity. We will notify you via email and/or a prominent notice on our Product of any change in ownership or uses of your personal information, as well as any choices you may have regarding your personal information.
privacy_special_hipaa: *** For covered medical professionals, LingoLinq operates as a Business Associate. User-generated content is encrypted in transit (SSL) and at rest. We will execute Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with eligible healthcare organizations upon request.
privacy_special_ferpa: *** When LingoLinq is used by schools, we act as a "School Official" with a legitimate educational interest. We maintain the confidentiality of student records and use data strictly to provide the contracted educational services.
privacy_special_coppa: *** Children under 13 may only use LingoLinq with verifiable consent from a parent, guardian, or authorized school official. If we learn we have collected personal information from a child under 13 without proper consent, we will delete it promptly.
privacy_special_disclaimer: *** While LingoLinq utilizes commercially acceptable, industry-standard means to protect your personal information, no method of transmission over the Internet or method of electronic storage is 100% secure. Therefore, we cannot guarantee its absolute security against sophisticated, unforeseen cyberattacks or zero-day vulnerabilities.
privacy_rights_heading: *** 6. International and State Privacy Rights (GDPR, CCPA)
privacy_rights_intro: *** Depending on your location, you have specific rights regarding your personal data. Where LingoLinq acts as a Data Controller (for direct, individual subscribers) or a Data Processor (for schools and clinics), we guarantee the following rights:
privacy_rights_access: *** You can request a copy of the personal data we hold about you.
privacy_rights_deletion_heading: *** Right to Deletion ("Right to be Forgotten"):
privacy_rights_deletion: *** You can request the permanent deletion of your account and personal data at any time.
privacy_rights_correction: *** You may update or correct inaccurate data within your profile settings.
privacy_rights_portability: *** You may request a secure export of your data in a structured, commonly used format.
privacy_rights_ccpa: *** LingoLinq does not sell your personal information, nor do we share it for cross-context behavioral advertising.
privacy_rights_contact: *** To exercise any of these rights, please contact us at support@lingolinq.com. We will respond within the timeframes required by applicable law.
privacy_security_heading: *** 7. Data Security, Retention, and Breach Notification
privacy_security_security: *** We utilize industry-standard encryption, secure cloud infrastructure, and strict internal access controls to protect your account.
privacy_security_retention: *** We retain active accounts indefinitely. Accounts inactive for 12 months are flagged for automatic deletion. Upon deletion, your personal data is purged (subject to a 10-day grace period for accidental deletions).
privacy_security_incident: *** In the unlikely event of a security breach that exposes personal information or results in data loss, LingoLinq will notify affected users and organization administrators via email within 72 hours of confirming the incident, providing details and a remediation plan.
privacy_thirdparty: *** The Product may contain links to or allow you to launch third-party websites, applications, or services (such as YouTube or external web pages) that are not operated by LingoLinq. If you click a third-party link, you will be directed to that third party's site. We have no control over and assume no responsibility for the content, privacy policies, or practices of any third-party sites or services. We strongly advise you to review the Privacy Policy of every site you visit.
privacy_changes: *** We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices or legal requirements. If we make a material change, we will provide you with prominent notice (email or an in-app notification) prior to the change becoming effective and update the "Last Updated" date at the top of this page.
privacy_contact_intro: *** If you have questions, data deletion requests, or compliance inquiries, please contact our Data Privacy Team:
pp_intro_1: *** LingoLinq is a powerful, flexible communication app and system that enables communicators and the teams around them to develop a personalized language learning strategy and to communicate effectively. Because LingoLinq is used in medical and educational settings for different ages of user, we are sensitive to state and federal regulations like FERPA, HIPAA, COPPA, etc. and work hard to track policies related to those regulations. Compliance with privacy and security regulations requires collaboration between LingoLinq and the institutions that use our software. As such, we have compiled this set of assertions and best practices to prevent exposing personal information to anyone who shouldn't have access to it.
pp_intro_2: *** LingoLinq uses the cloud to back up, synchronize, and report on a communicator's vocabulary and activities. We do this to provide convenience for users (backup and multi-device support), insights on communicator progress, collaboration across support teams, accountability for organizations, and general trends across the site. Because of the potentially sensitive nature of the information related to an individual's communication, we take user privacy very seriously. Below are some of our protection strategies, and best practices that you can follow to ensure the privacy and rights of the communicator are respected. The information is provided to help organizations in their decision-making and training processes, and may change over time.
pp_personal_pre: *** By default LingoLinq tries to collect as little personal information as possible about our users. At registration we ask for a username and email address, and we record the initial IP address for location tracking purposes. Any additional information provided by the user is optional and opt-in. Some features of LingoLinq, if enabled, will result in additional levels of tracking and information storage. For example, logging records additional data as the user uses the system, and the personalization of boards results in the storage of additional images and data fields based on the user-entered information.
pp_personal_bold: *** We encourage therapy and educational teams to discuss together what information is appropriate to be added for an individual user
pp_general_pre: *** By default LingoLinq doesn't collect personal or academic information about our users. Access to LingoLinq is login-based, and every user must have a user name, email address, and password. However, the email address can be reused or even be invalid if needed.
pp_general_bold: *** We encourage therapy and educational teams who create logins on behalf of their users to use anonymized user names
pp_general_post: *** and many programs already have anonymized identifiers in place for the users they work with.
pp_user_data_1_pre: *** The LingoLinq application communicates with remote servers to download and update user-generated information such as board content, logs, etc. This communication is always done over a secure, encrypted (SSL) channel. In addition, user-generated content such as buttons, email address, profile information and log data is all treated as potentially private and personal information, and is encrypted before being stored to prevent unauthorized access. Most pages within LingoLinq can potentially contain private information, so rather than use confidential information warnings on every page,
pp_user_data_1_bold: *** we encourage organizations to treat all LingoLinq access as potentially private and confidential
pp_user_data_2_pre: *** Within the system users can specify that their account is "public", in which case basic user-entered information like summary, public boards, etc. will be available to any LingoLinq users, but this is an opt-in behavior.
pp_user_data_2_bold: *** We discourage communicator accounts from being set to public.
pp_user_data_2_post: *** The user name tied to each account is not encrypted, and without authorization another LingoLinq user can check on the existence of a specific user name, but will not be able to retrieve any additional non-public information about that user name. This is another reason why we encourage teams to use anonymized user names when creating accounts for their communicators.
pp_user_data_3_pre: *** Administrative access within LingoLinq is limited to only those who need direct access to fulfil their work responsibilities. LingoLinq employees and subcontractors with potential access to personal data are trained on user privacy best practices and are instructed to only access information needed for supporting communicators and teams. Within the app, access to user information is based on strict access controls, and any access to a communicator's information must be authorized by the communicator account. The only exception to this is if an organization creates communicator accounts and assigns them to communicators, in which case
pp_user_data_3_bold: *** we encourage organizations to make sure communicators are aware of and comfortable with the organization's access to their information before proceeding.
pp_user_data_4_pre: *** Because communication is personal and individualized, many communicators add buttons representing personal information, such as family members, medical details, addresses, etc. The system does not prevent this type of information from being added, but it is not required. Such user-generated data will be encrypted, but is still available once logged in.
pp_user_data_4_bold: *** Support teams should talk with communicators before adding potentially sensitive information to their boards, and should remember that this information could technically be discovered by anyone with physical access to the communicator's device.
pp_user_data_5_pre: *** It is important to note that user-uploaded files including images (including photographs), audio records and videos uploaded to the LingoLinq system are encrypted in transit via SSL, but are not encrypted at rest (although they are protected from unintentional access using long randomly-generated identifiers), and
pp_user_data_5_bold: *** we suggest only uploading anonymized images and videos that do not disclose private information
pp_logs_1_pre: *** In addition, communicators can add "supervisors" to their account. Supervisors are additional logins that are used to a different person, possibly a therapist, parent, teacher, grandparent, aide, etc. Supervisors can be added as read-only or with permission to edit a communicator's boards. All supervisors have access to a communicator's full vocabulary set and any logs that have been recorded. As such,
pp_logs_1_bold: *** we encourage support teams to check with communicators before adding anyone as a supervisor to their account on their behalf
pp_logs_2_pre: *** LingoLinq has a built-in logging and reporting mechanism that can provide valuable insights and summaries of communication usage and progress over time. Data can be a powerful tool as support teams try to assess a communicator's progress across multiple environments and times of day. However, logging every button a communicator selects is a
pp_logs_2_bold2: *** support teams should get explicit permission from a communicator before enabling logging on their behalf.
pp_logs_2_post: *** There are two levels of logging in LingoLinq, general logging which records every action in a user's communication session, and an additional level which also tracks GPS locations to be used for filtering data based on physical location. Both levels are opt-in, and LingoLinq includes a user-controlled mechanism which can permanently delete all previous logs generated in the system (this purge can take up to 24 hours). You can see what information is recorded via logging in our
pp_logs_3: *** LingoLinq incorporates anonymized data from all user-generated logs to share usage trends such as most common words, core vs. fringe breakdown, etc. These public trends are always strictly anonymized and not gathered without enough different user sources to ensure individual user information is protected. When users enable logging they can opt-in to allowing their usage log information to be anonymized and shared with third-party research groups. Personally-identifiable information, including email addresses, personalized phrases or location information, will not be shared with outside research parties without explicit user consent.
pp_third_party_1: *** Some components of LingoLinq take advantage of third-party services to improve the user experience. LingoLinq reports send anonymized data to the Google Charts service to generate visualizations of usage over time. LingoLinq uses Google Analytics to track user trends and to help evaluate the effectiveness of new features. These third-party services are opt-in, and the actions that enable these services are clearly delineated within the system.
pp_third_party_2_pre: *** Additionally, LingoLinq "launches" players for third party content including YouTube, Tarheel Reader and OpenAAC. By default these launches do not send any LingoLinq-stored information unless clearly specified when setting up the tool for a user. These third-party services may include their own tracking mechanisms, and can be included as button launches on user boards. LingoLinq also allows for "launches" from arbitrary web sites based on user-entered URLs. Control over whether to allow third-party launches is available in a user's preferences, and
pp_third_party_2_bold: *** we encourage teams concerned about external tracking to disable third-party launches for their users
pp_third_party_3_pre: *** We use the server-based troubleshooting and logging services listed in our
pp_third_party_3_mid: *** to aid in application troubleshooting and information security, which send limited user metadata such as IP Address and User Agent, but this data is deleted after 7-14 days. Organization-created communicator accounts have error tracking disabled by default for everything other than IP address (which we keep to use to combat fraud and maintain information security), so
pp_third_party_3_bold: *** we encourage organizations to create user accounts through the organization interface, or to manually disable error tracking in a user's preferences if there are concerns about user metadata being stored outside the system
pp_third_party_4_pre: *** In addition, LingoLinq collects contact information when users sign up or purchase the app. This information is used for support and marketing purposes and is stored in third-party systems that LingoLinq uses for communication and support. The information shared includes name, email address and IP address. However, organization-created communicator accounts are not shared with third-party communication services, so
pp_third_party_4_bold: *** we encourage organizations to create user accounts through the organization interface to prevent email addresses from being shared
pp_third_party_4_post: *** with these third-party services. If your users are not created this way, you can disable this setting in your user preferences and we will remove your information from our marketing tools.
pp_third_party_5_pre: *** LingoLinq can optionally send out notifications to communicators and supervisors. These notifications include things like weekly usage summaries, notifications of badges earned, or messages sent by the communicator from within the app. It is possible that information sent in these notifications will contain user-generated information such as buttons pressed or goals set. These notifications can be sent via email, SMS, or as alerts on the user's dashboard. Email is the default notification policy.
pp_third_party_5_bold: *** If private information has been added to boards or used in creating goals or other such systems, we encourage communicators and supervisors to set their notification preferences to remain within the app so as to prevent the unwanted exposure of user information.
pp_session_pre: *** LingoLinq is accessible from mobile and Windows apps, or from any modern web browser. Access requires entering the user's user name and password before being granted access to the user's interface, which will include their own content and the content of any users who have added them as a supervisor. When accessing from a web browser, the user session will expire by default after 24 hours of inactivity unless otherwise specified by the user. The user can opt-in to a longer timeout which will expire after multiple days of inactivity.
pp_session_bold1: *** To help protect user information, we encourage browser-based logins to use the shorter timeout, and to manually log out after each session.
pp_session_mid: *** App-based logins use the longer timeout by default, so
pp_session_bold2: *** we encourage app-based logins to set up a device-level PIN or password to prevent unauthorized access through the physical device.
pp_backup_pre: *** LingoLinq databases are backed up regularly with the same encryption as the live database. File uploads by users are backed up to multiple facilities by our data storage partners. In the event of a catastrophic event, or breach or misconfiguration resulting in data loss, LingoLinq does not guarantee that user information and content will be retrievable, but LingoLinq will work in a commercially reasonable manner to restore any and all lost information. Any total loss of informatin will be communicated to the affected parties within 72 hours. For more information please see our
pp_removing_1: *** LingoLinq logs and board provide ongoing value, so for active users this information is not deleted. Users may choose to delete their usage logs in their entirety at any time, or delete their full account including boards and logs, from within their profile. When an account deletion is requested we delay the deletion for up to 18 days to allow for cancellations or mistakes. Some users take advantage of LingoLinq's features only seasonally, so we wait a full year of inactivity before initiating the process of automatically deleting a user's profile, but users can always request the account to be removed sooner if they would like. Accounts created by organizations are not deleted until requested by the organization, or after the termination of the contract. When an account is deleted, boards and logs are removed as well, but historical aggregate data generated using those data sources will not be updated, as this aggregate data does not expose user-specific information.
pp_removing_2: *** An organization may, as part of their transition to another service, wish to migrate their data out of LingoLinq. On an as-needed basis we will work with these organizations to create a standard export of all organization and user data that is recorded within LingoLinq. Such an export will contain only information directly tied to the organization, and only for users created by the organization. Users who sign up for their own accounts are are later added to the organization will need to grant permission on a one-by-one basis before their information can be included in an organization export.
pp_requests_pre: *** On request, we can provide information about accounts for support or general usage purpose. By default we will only provide this information to someone tied directly to the specified account (i.e. with a matching email address), or is authorized within LingoLinq to supervise the account. Organizations can define users as administrators within the LingoLinq app, and will then also be allowed to request information for users within their organization. If a parent or other user who is not authorized within LingoLinq requests information, we will verify their authorization with the organization tied to the user's account. If the user is not tied to an organization, we will confirm with the user account directly before sharing information about the user. We do not share non-anonymizeed data with third parties other than what is recorded in the
pp_security_pre: *** We have many security measures in place to protect against unauthorized access to user information, including training our employees on privacy and encrypting and obfuscating data sources. However, as we have seen in recent years even strict security measures are at times compromised. In the event that personal user information is exposed to unapproved parties, or LingoLinq becomes aware of unauthorized access to our internal system resources, we will notify affected users via email within 72 hours, unless organization partners agree upon a different notification process. If comprehensive information is not available at the time of the report we will include a schedule of updates, not less often than one update per week, until the issue has been resolved or concluded. Please also refer to our
pp_closing: *** At LingoLinq we work hard to ensure communicators are respected and given the privacy that everyone deserves. If you have questions about these policies please don't hesitate to reach out to us.

faq_ai_boards_q: *** What are some interesting and engaging speech boards I can create using AI board generation?
faq_ai_boards_p1: *** AI board generation turns a short description into a starter layout you can edit—buttons, groups, and paths you refine like any other board. The most engaging boards are tied to real life: a specific routine, place, person, or goal, with vocabulary the communicator will actually want to use that week.
faq_ai_boards_p2: *** Try prompting for situations, not just categories. Instead of only "food words," describe "ordering lunch in the cafeteria" or "choosing a snack after school." Mix core words (want, help, more, stop) with fringe words for that moment (allergy, spicy, debit card, teammate). That balance keeps boards useful in conversation, not just as a static word list.
faq_ai_boards_list_intro: *** Ideas that work well in classrooms and clinics:
faq_ai_boards_li_1: *** Daily living: morning routine, chores, homework, bedtime—each with a small set of predictable phrases.
faq_ai_boards_li_2: *** Social participation: playground games, club meetings, video calls with family, small talk with neighbors.
faq_ai_boards_li_3: *** Community access: grocery store, restaurant, pharmacy, library—scripts for questions, choices, and problem-solving.
faq_ai_boards_li_4: *** Learning: science vocabulary for a unit, math talk (estimate, compare, prove), field trip safety and participation.
faq_ai_boards_li_5: *** Play and hobbies: rules and turns for favorite games, sports cheers, art or music lesson requests.
faq_ai_boards_li_6: *** Regulation and health: calming choices, pain or comfort scale, explaining symptoms, allergy and medication phrases.
faq_ai_boards_p3: *** After generation, edit ruthlessly: rename buttons in the communicator's voice, swap symbols so they read quickly, and link back to a stable home or backup board. Start with one situation that matters this month, then duplicate and adapt once it feels comfortable.
faq_aac_q: *** What Is AAC? (A Simple Guide for Parents & Caregivers)
faq_aac_intro_p1: *** If your child—or someone you care for—has difficulty speaking, you may have heard the term AAC. It can feel overwhelming at first, but AAC is simply about helping people communicate in the way that works best for them.
faq_aac_intro_p2: *** This guide will walk you through what AAC means, who it’s for, the different types available, and how tools like LingoLinq fit into the picture.
faq_aac_stand_for_line: *** AAC stands for Augmentative and Alternative Communication.
faq_aac_simple_body: *** AAC includes any method of communication that helps someone express themselves if speaking is difficult or not possible.
faq_aac_not_just: *** AAC is not just for people who “can’t talk”—it’s for anyone who needs support communicating more effectively.
faq_aac_who_intro: *** AAC is used by people of all ages, from young children to adults. It can support individuals with:
faq_aac_who_duration: *** Some people use AAC short-term, while others rely on it throughout their lives.
faq_aac_important_body: *** Using AAC does not stop someone from learning to speak. In many cases, it actually supports and improves speech development.
faq_aac_types_intro: *** AAC can be broken into two main categories:
faq_aac_high_tech_desc: *** These are electronic tools or apps that help people communicate.
faq_aac_how_p1: *** Most AAC systems are built around a communication board—a layout of buttons, symbols, or words.
faq_aac_how_p2: *** Over time, users learn where words are located and how to navigate quickly—just like typing on a keyboard.
faq_aac_ll_intro: *** LingoLinq is part of the next generation of AAC tools—focused not just on communication, but on improving how communication happens.

privacy_special_coppa_v2: *** Children under 13 may only use LingoLinq with verifiable parental consent. We accept a FERPA school-official authorization in place of direct parental consent only for the limited, school-curriculum use of LingoLinq with no AI features, no profiling, and no advertising. Any use of LingoLinq's AI features by a child under 13, including AI-assisted board generation and AI word prediction, requires verifiable parental consent under 16 CFR Part 312, regardless of school enrollment. If we learn we have collected personal information from a child under 13 without the required consent, we will delete it promptly.
privacy_special_ai_consent_intro: *** Because using LingoLinq's word prediction sends some information to an outside AI company, we ask for a separate, second AI data-sharing consent beyond the general parental consent described above, specific to that feature. AI-drafted evaluation summaries are currently inactive and send nothing to any AI company; that feature produces a draft on our own systems instead, and turning on live AI evaluation summaries would require an updated disclosure and a fresh consent before anything is sent. You do not have to agree to this second consent to use the rest of LingoLinq. See our
privacy_security_retention_intro: *** We retain personal data only as long as necessary for the purpose it was collected, with category-specific windows that align with our Data Retention Schedule.
privacy_security_retention_active: *** Active account data: retained for the life of the account, plus up to 2 years of continuous inactivity, after which the account is soft-deleted and queued for purge.
privacy_security_retention_inactive: *** Inactive accounts: accounts inactive for 12 months are flagged for automatic deletion, subject to a 10-day grace period for accidental deletions.
privacy_security_retention_ai_logs: *** AI request logs: the audit record (AiApiLog) is retained for 2 years; IP addresses on those records are redacted at 90 days.
privacy_security_retention_ai_eu: *** AI request logs for accounts in the European Union: retained up to 5 years, already in effect, to meet EU AI Act Article 50 record-keeping requirements.
privacy_security_retention_voice: *** Voice and audio recordings (button sounds you record): retained for the life of the user account and deleted when the account is deleted.
privacy_security_retention_dwell: *** Dwell, eye-gaze, and head-tracking timing data (stored within communication logs): retained for 3 years by default, configurable to a shorter window per user or organization.
privacy_security_retention_tenant: *** School and district tenant data: deleted within 90 days after the customer contract ends, unless a shorter window is specified in the data processing addendum.
privacy_security_retention_children: *** Children's data (users under 13): parent-controllable at any time; automatically purged at age 18 or after 2 years of inactivity, whichever is sooner. Verified parental deletion requests are processed within 30 days.
privacy_security_retention_backups: *** Backups follow a 35-day rolling window for operational recovery; if a record is deleted, our retention jobs re-apply the deletion after any restore. The full schedule, including legal basis and deletion mechanism for each category, is available on request from our Data Privacy Team.

privacy_beta_notice_body: *** This notice applies while LingoLinq is in beta and expires at general launch. During the beta, LingoLinq is pre-release software provided "as is." Please keep your primary communication method available at all times, and do not rely on LingoLinq as your only means of communication during this period. If you opt in, authorized staff may review anonymized, diagnostic usage data to fix bugs and improve accessibility; consistent with our Private Thoughts Guarantee, we do not review the words or sentences a communicator generates. For users under 13, verifiable parental consent (or, for school use, school-official authorization) is required before any data is collected. If you use LingoLinq with real patient information, your organization should have a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) in place with us first; contact us to execute one. You can request deletion of your account at any time, and deletion timing follows the retention windows described in Section 7 below.

privacy_sharing_ai: *** for AI-assisted board suggestions, word prediction, and, only when a speech-language pathologist takes a separate action to request it, AI-drafted evaluation summaries;
privacy_sharing_ai_vendors: *** When enabled, LingoLinq's AI features use Anthropic's Claude models hosted on Amazon Bedrock, inside a LingoLinq-controlled AWS account under a signed Business Associate Agreement (Claude Haiku 4.5 for AI-assisted board suggestions and word prediction). Today none of these features send any user content to an AI vendor, because the Bedrock path is inactive. AI-drafted evaluation summaries are inactive for a second, separate reason: that feature sends nothing to any AI vendor even when the Bedrock path is active, and produces a draft written on our own systems instead. Before anything is sent to any AI vendor, we automatically filter out common identifying details we can detect, such as names, emails, phone numbers, and account identifiers; this filter is not perfect, and we describe the result as scrubbed or pseudonymized data, not the formal legal standard for removing all identifying information. On Amazon Bedrock the model provider does not receive this information at all, and AWS states it is not used to train any model. AWS may retain it for a limited period for safety and abuse prevention, so we do not currently claim a zero-data-retention guarantee for this path.
privacy_sharing_ai_disclosure_link_intro: *** For the full AI data-sharing disclosure, including exactly what is sent for each AI feature and how to give or withdraw consent, see our
privacy_special_ai_consent_outro: *** for the full details and how to give or withdraw this consent.
privacy_special_ai_board_suggestions_not: *** AI-assisted board suggestions (for example, typing a topic like "the zoo" to get word ideas) are not covered by this second consent. LingoLinq automatically removes names and other identifying details from that topic text before it is used, and the topic itself is ordinarily just a subject, not information about your child.
privacy_security_retention_ai_children: *** AI request logs for accounts belonging to a child under 13: a rolling 12 months, independent of account status. This window has been decided and is being put into effect.
privacy_security_retention_ai_general: *** AI request logs for all other accounts: 24 months. This window has been decided and is being put into effect.
